scams.name: KLIA/KLIA2 'Teksi Sapu' Airport Taxi Overcharge & Grab-Cancellation Scam
scams.description: Kuala Lumpur International Airport's two terminals (KLIA Terminal 1 and KLIA2) host Malaysia's most-documented 2025 taxi-overcharge ecosystem — the locally-named 'teksi sapu' (literally 'sweeper taxi') are unlicensed touts who intercept arriving foreigners in arrivals halls and charge 3–6x the legitimate fare. r/KualaLumpur '11 Scams in Kuala Lumpur to Avoid' (comments/1odz6b8, 2025) is the community baseline. r/malaysia 'KLIA teksi sapu predators continue to fleece unsuspecting tourists' (comments/13dqnv7, 2023) established the recurring pattern. r/malaysia 'Taxi Driver charged me 3x the price of a Grab ride' (comments/1f02xsk, 2024) and r/KualaLumpur 'Scary Grab experience in KL — warning for other travellers' (comments/1npv0w4, 2025) are first-person 2024–2025 anchors. r/malaysia 'At KLIA 2 Grab cancel 6 Times, 1 say Tiada Minyak' (comments/1bjfhg9, 2024) documents the Grab-cancellation overlay. On 7 October 2025, New Straits Times reported a Bruneian single mother was fined RM 5,000 by a magistrate after pleading guilty to charging a tourist RM 836 for an illegal taxi ride from KLIA2 — the Malay Mail headline 'Repeat KLIA2 tout fined RM 5,000 for overcharging tourist RM 836 for illegal taxi ride' confirmed she was a repeat offender. The legitimate KLIA-to-KL-city Grab fare is RM 65–RM 95 (airport surcharge included); the KLIA Ekspres train is RM 55 one-way, 33 minutes to KL Sentral. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) unbadged men in arrivals halls approach visibly-foreign travellers with 'taxi? hotel? Bukit Bintang?' — NO legitimate driver solicits in the terminal; (b) quoted prices of RM 250–RM 500 for rides that cost RM 65–RM 95 on Grab, sometimes 'limo' pitches of RM 400+; (c) Grab driver accepts your in-app ride, then messages 'app broken, cash please' or 'cancel lah, I drive you RM 150 cash' — (comments/1dh8dyd, 2024) and r/malaysia 'Grab driver asking me to cancel ride, is it safe?' (comments/1fy5khc, 2024); (d) luggage held hostage at destination with RM 200+ 'surcharge' demands — r/malaysia 'Taxi driver demanding money for seat belt being stuck' (comments/1932t8q, 2024) documents fabricated-charge extortion; (e) counterfeit 'coupon taxi' counters upstairs at KLIA2 selling rides at RM 200+ when the real budget coupon-taxi to KL city is RM 84.30 (fixed by JPJ). For travelers: (1) IGNORE every 'taxi?' approach inside KLIA or KLIA2 arrivals — all legitimate transport is downstairs at the BUDGET/PREMIER taxi coupon counter or via Grab at the signposted pickup zone; (2) book Grab on airport Wi-Fi AFTER collecting luggage — Terminal 1 pickup is Level 3 Gate 8/9; KLIA2 pickup is Level 1 Block A/B Door 3 — RM 65–RM 95 to central hotels; (3) alternative: KLIA Ekspres train from the station INSIDE the terminal to KL Sentral is RM 55 one-way, 33 minutes, every 20 minutes from 5 AM to 12:30 AM — safest budget option; (4) if you must use a coupon taxi, buy ONLY at the official 'Budget/Premier Taxi' counter in arrivals (look for the government JPJ logo) — fixed fare to KL city is RM 84.30 (budget) or RM 118.30 (premier); NEVER negotiate with anyone walking around; (5) if your Grab driver asks you to cancel, you cancel the ride yourself (no fee when driver initiates) and rebook — (comments/1npv0w4, 2025); (6) never hand cash upfront — Grab is in-app payment only; (7) photograph the car's number plate before loading luggage; (8) report teksi sapu to JPJ hotline 1-800-88-7723 or MOTAC tourist hotline 1300-88-5050; on 2 December 2025 The Sun reported a foreigner was hit with a 'ridiculously high limo fare at KLIA1' — incidents continue through 2026.
scams.avoidance:
IGNORE every 'taxi?' approach in arrivals — all legitimate transport is at the BUDGET/PREMIER coupon counter or the signposted Grab pickup zone
Book Grab on airport Wi-Fi after luggage — RM 65–RM 95 to central KL
OR take KLIA Ekspres train inside the terminal — RM 55, 33 minutes to KL Sentral
If Grab driver asks you to cancel, you cancel yourself and rebook; never pay cash upfront
Report teksi sapu to JPJ 1-800-88-7723 or MOTAC 1300-88-5050
scams.location: KLIA Terminal 1 arrivals, KLIA2 arrivals Level 3, coupon-taxi counter queues, Grab pickup zones Terminal 1 Level 3 Gate 8/9 and KLIA2 Level 1 Block A/B, KL Sentral hotel drop-offs

scams.name: Petronas Twin Towers Skybridge Fake 'Sold Out' Ticket Tout Scam
scams.description: The Petronas Twin Towers Skybridge and Observation Deck is KL's single highest-footfall tourist attraction, with around 1,500 daily ticketed visitors and chronic sell-outs — conditions perfect for the 'sold out' counterfeit-ticket scam that operates at the KLCC Suria mall concourse and the KLCC Park entrance fountains. r/KualaLumpur '11 Scams in Kuala Lumpur to Avoid' (comments/1odz6b8, 2025) lists this as a staple 2025 scam. r/KualaLumpur 'What's the most common scam / tourist traps found in-and-around KL' (comments/1cknwtp, 2024) and r/malaysia 'Common scams in Malaysia I should be aware about?' (comments/19b72r4, 2024) document the 'sold out, but I can get you in' pitch at the tower base. The legitimate ticket price is RM 98 for non-Malaysian adults (Level 41 Skybridge + Level 86 Observation Deck combo), sold ONLY at the Concourse-level Petronas ticket counter inside Tower 2 (lower ground floor, through KLCC LRT station entrance) or at petronastwintowers.com.my — same-day tickets usually sell out by 11 AM; bookings open 3 days in advance online. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) a well-dressed local (often in a shirt with vague 'tour guide' or 'hospitality' branding) intercepts tourists approaching the tower base between 9 AM and 2 PM, claiming 'tickets finished for today lah, but I have VIP allocation through my company'; (b) quoted prices of RM 200–RM 500 per person for what are claimed to be 'private tour' or 'corporate allocation' tickets — sometimes backed by a real-looking printed confirmation with QR code; (c) the QR codes are either recycled from yesterday's used tickets, photoshopped stock images, or redirect to phishing sites that capture card details; (d) variant: tout directs tourists to a 'partner' travel agency in Avenue K or Intermark Mall across the road, where the 'tour package' includes the fake ticket plus a gem-shop visit (linked to the Chinatown gem investment scam pattern); (e) r/KualaLumpur 'Did I just get scammed?' (comments/1m57t6f, 2025) and r/KualaLumpur 'URGENT help needed, I think I got scammed for RM 6k' (comments/1mh4amt, 2025) document larger 'tour package' escalations that start with the 'sold out tower' pitch. For travelers: (1) check availability yourself at petronastwintowers.com.my BEFORE leaving your hotel — if tickets show online, they are available; even 'sold out' days usually have a physical walk-up queue released from 8:30 AM at the Concourse counter; (2) ALL legitimate tickets are sold at ONE location — the Concourse-level counter inside Tower 2 with Petronas branding and uniformed staff in burgundy blazers — nowhere else on the property; (3) NEVER buy tickets from anyone approaching you in KLCC Park, KLCC Suria mall, the LRT station concourse, or the pedestrian bridges; (4) if you genuinely miss out, the Skybridge View Deck at KL Tower (Menara KL) offers a comparable city view including the Petronas Towers themselves in the frame — RM 110 for foreigners and almost never sells out; (5) photo alternatives: KLCC Park lake at dusk (free), Heli Lounge Bar at Menara KH (free entry, drinks RM 35+), or the public rooftop of Isetan The Japan Store at Lot 10; (6) refuse every 'private tour package' combining tower tickets with shopping — these are universally scams; (7) if you paid a tout and have not yet scanned the QR, contest the charge immediately with your bank AND file a police report at KLCC police beat (Pavilion KL basement or KLCC LRT police kiosk); (8) save MOTAC tourist hotline 1300-88-5050 for English-language assistance with ticket disputes.
scams.avoidance:
Check availability yourself at petronastwintowers.com.my before leaving your hotel
Buy ONLY at the Concourse-level counter inside Tower 2 with Petronas burgundy-blazer staff
NEVER buy from anyone in KLCC Park, Suria mall or the LRT concourse
Fallback: KL Tower (Menara KL) RM 110, or free views at KLCC Park lake and Lot 10 rooftop
Refuse all 'private tour + shopping' combo packages — universally scams
scams.location: Petronas Twin Towers base, KLCC Suria mall Concourse level, KLCC Park entrances, KLCC LRT station concourse, Avenue K and Intermark Mall pedestrian bridges, Jalan P. Ramlee tourist approach

scams.name: Central Market & Chinatown Gem Investment Confidence Scam
scams.description: KL's Central Market (Pasar Seni) and the surrounding Chinatown/Petaling Street grid host the Southeast Asian gem-investment confidence scam that has plagued Bangkok, Colombo, and Jaipur for decades — transplanted to Malaysia with a 'Malaysia-grown sapphire, no export duty' pitch. r/KualaLumpur '11 Scams in Kuala Lumpur to Avoid' (comments/1odz6b8, 2025) identifies the gem scam as a top-five KL tourist scam. r/KualaLumpur 'URGENT help needed, I think I got scammed for RM 6k' (comments/1mh4amt, 2025) is a 2025 first-person anchor where a tourist was walked from Central Market to a 'certified' gem dealer and paid RM 6,000 for glass. r/KualaLumpur 'Scammer Alert in KL — Lost $300 USD in a Street Scam (Please read)' (comments/1k3umhl, 2025) and r/KualaLumpur 'Did I just get scammed?' (comments/1m57t6f, 2025) document smaller-scale versions of the same pattern. r/malaysia 'PSA: Common scams, their modus operandi and tips on how to avoid them' (comments/r957ss, 2021) is the community's canonical reference document. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) a friendly, English-fluent 'local' approaches a tourist at Central Market, the Pasar Seni LRT exit, or on Jalan Petaling — typical opener is 'where are you from?' followed by claims of having family in your country; (b) conversation pivots to 'I can show you a real Malaysian gem shop — government-licensed, not tourist prices' and offers a free tuk-tuk/Grab ride to a 'friend's' shop in the Sultan Street area, Jalan Tun H. S. Lee, or occasionally the Mid Valley gem wholesale corridor; (c) at the shop, a 'gemologist' in a white coat produces certificates stamped with fake GIA, AIGS, or 'Gem Society of Malaysia' logos — Malaysia has NO national gem certification body and is NOT a significant gemstone producer (sapphires are not meaningfully mined in Peninsular Malaysia); (d) tourist is shown sapphires, rubies, or 'royal Malaysian jade' priced at RM 1,500–RM 25,000, with claims of 3x resale value in Europe/US; (e) stones are glass, synthetic corundum, or cheap sillimanite worth RM 20–RM 200 wholesale; (f) credit-card cloning variant — card 'held for deposit' during paperwork is skimmed; (g) r/malaysia 'Got scammed at Ria Money Exchange in Bukit Bintang' (comments/1obs731, 2025) shows the broader 2025 confidence-scam ecosystem in KL. For travelers: (1) NEVER follow any stranger who approaches you asking 'where are you from?' to a second location — this is the universal tell of a confidence scam; (2) there is NO legitimate investment-grade gem trade in Malaysia — unlike Thailand's Chanthaburi or Sri Lanka's Ratnapura, Malaysia is not a gemstone-producing country of note; (3) Central Market itself is a legitimate craft market — buy songket, batik, pewter, and handicrafts there, but NEVER follow anyone OUT of the market; (4) the 'certificates' are meaningless — real gem certification (GIA, GRS, AGL) is done in the United States, Switzerland, or Thailand, not issued by Malaysian retail shops; (5) NEVER hand your credit card for 'deposit' or 'paperwork' at any Malaysian shop — pay by Visa/Mastercard at the register only, watching the terminal; (6) if you've already paid, contact your bank for chargeback IMMEDIATELY (within 24 hours) citing 'merchant misrepresentation' and file a report at KPDN (consumer protection) hotline 1-800-886-800 or ezadu.kpdn.gov.my; (7) file a PDRM police report at IPD Dang Wangi (central KL's downtown police station, +60 3-2697 2222) — a police report is required for most bank chargeback claims; (8) save KPDN (Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri) online complaint portal and the tourist hotline 1300-88-5050 for English-language help; (comments/1mh4amt, 2025), the bank chargeback succeeded when the victim acted within 48 hours.
scams.avoidance:
NEVER follow any stranger who asks 'where are you from?' to a second location
Malaysia has no legitimate investment-grade gem industry — assume all such pitches are scams
Central Market is fine for songket, batik, pewter — but never follow anyone OUT of the market
Never hand your credit card for 'deposit' — pay at register only, watching the terminal
File bank chargeback + PDRM report at IPD Dang Wangi +60 3-2697 2222 within 24 hours; KPDN hotline 1-800-886-800
scams.location: Central Market (Pasar Seni), Jalan Petaling/Chinatown, Jalan Tun H. S. Lee, Sultan Street gem-shop cluster, Pasar Seni LRT exit, Mid Valley wholesale corridor, Kasturi Walk pedestrian strip

scams.name: Fake Plainclothes Police 'Passport & Wallet Inspection' Shakedown
scams.description: KL's plainclothes fake-police shakedown targets foreign tourists on the Jalan Petaling (Chinatown), Bukit Bintang, Masjid Jamek, and Chow Kit pedestrian corridors, with a 2024–2025 escalation into KLCC pedestrian zones. r/KualaLumpur '11 Scams in Kuala Lumpur to Avoid' (comments/1odz6b8, 2025) names this as a core KL scam. r/KualaLumpur 'Alert a scam in KL by foreigns' (comments/1o20sxg, 2025) is a 2025 community-warning anchor. r/KualaLumpur 'Almost got scammed by Grab Driver and Uniformed police' (comments/1nfcpmt, 2025) documents the rarer Grab-plus-fake-police team-up. r/malaysia 'PDRM asking for IC and searching phone for specific terms' (comments/1h3ujxq, 2024) establishes the real-vs-fake detection baseline. On 4 November 2025 Malay Mail reported 'Two men fined RM 5,000 each for impersonating traffic police, demanding money from teens in Ipoh' — confirming the pattern extends across Malaysia. On Thesun.my (November 2025) police arrested a man for impersonating a police officer committing robbery and obscenity, and Makkal Osai reported 'Two men posing as immigration officers arrested for extorting foreigners'. The 2025 shakedown pattern: (a) two men in plain clothes approach a tourist — often a solo walker or small group — and flash a laminated badge (often a generic 'POLIS' or 'Immigration' card), claiming a 'drug check' or 'passport inspection'; (b) they demand to see passport and wallet 'for narcotics inspection' or 'to verify you carry no counterfeit ringgit'; (c) once the wallet is surrendered, foreign cash (USD/EUR/SGD) is pocketed 'as evidence' and the wallet returned lighter — or card details are photographed on the spot; (d) phone-check variant: officer takes the unlocked phone and navigates to banking apps, demanding a transfer to an 'inspection account' — this is the locally-named 'Macau scam' street variant, distinct from the phone-call Macau scam; (e) some scammers wear semi-official-looking reflective vests and lurk near LRT stations (Masjid Jamek, Pasar Seni, Bukit Bintang) and approach tourists exiting after dark; (f) r/KualaLumpur 'I got tricked outside Masjid Jamek Sultan Abdulsamad' (comments/1ckfhtz, 2024) and r/KualaLumpur 'Got stopped by a muslim guy in (Publika)' (comments/1ktg00d, 2025) are 2024–2025 anchors. Critically: legitimate PDRM officers in plain clothes do NOT demand cash inspections on the street; real checks happen at an IPD (district police headquarters), NOT on a pavement. For travelers: (1) real PDRM officers will show an authorisation card (Kad Kuasa) with full name, rank, and badge number — ASK TO SEE IT and PHOTOGRAPH it; fake scammers refuse; (2) firmly state 'I want to go to the nearest IPD' (police station) — real officers comply; fake ones leave; (3) NEVER surrender your passport — carry a laminated photocopy for checks and keep the original in your hotel safe; (4) NEVER hand over your wallet or unlock your phone for any 'inspection' — decline politely; (5) call 999 (Malaysia's emergency number) in front of them — fake scammers disperse at the mere dial tone; (6) save these: PDRM Dang Wangi district (covers KLCC/Bukit Bintang) +60 3-2697 2222; IPD Brickfields (covers KL Sentral) +60 3-2272 6222; MOTAC tourist hotline 1300-88-5050 (English, 24/7); (7) if shakedown occurs and cash is stolen, go directly to the nearest IPD and file a report within 24 hours — required for travel-insurance claims and card disputes; (8) your embassy can assist — US Embassy KL +60 3-2168 5000, British High Commission +60 3-2170 2200, Canadian High Commission +60 3-2718 3333; (9) walk with confidence and make eye contact — scammers target visibly-disoriented-looking tourists (comments/1o20sxg, 2025).
scams.avoidance:
Ask to see and PHOTOGRAPH any officer's Kad Kuasa (authorisation card) with name + rank
State firmly 'I want to go to the nearest IPD (police station)' — real officers comply
NEVER surrender passport (carry a laminated photocopy) or unlock your phone for 'inspection'
Call 999 in front of them — fake scammers disperse at the dial tone
PDRM Dang Wangi +60 3-2697 2222; MOTAC tourist hotline 1300-88-5050 (English, 24/7)
scams.location: Jalan Petaling (Chinatown), Bukit Bintang pedestrian corridors, Masjid Jamek LRT exit, Pasar Seni LRT surrounds, Chow Kit night market, KLCC Park evening walkways, Jalan Alor food street

scams.name: Batu Caves Garland, Photographer & 'Temple Donation' Markup Scam
scams.description: The Batu Caves Hindu temple complex and its iconic 272 rainbow stairs receive approximately 2 million foreign tourists annually, and a small but persistent vendor fringe operates the 'gift-then-invoice', unofficial-photographer, and 'temple donation' markup trio at the base of the stairs and along the stair climb. r/KualaLumpur '11 Scams in Kuala Lumpur to Avoid' (comments/1odz6b8, 2025) lists Batu Caves vendor tactics in its 2025 summary. r/KualaLumpur 'What's the most common scam / tourist traps found in-and-around KL' (comments/1cknwtp, 2024) and r/KualaLumpur 'Beggars everywhere in Kuala Lumpur' (comments/1ml136o, 2025) document the broader KL tourist-overcharge pattern that extends to Batu Caves. r/KualaLumpur 'Fake beggers?' (comments/1kc3rug, 2025) and r/KualaLumpur 'So many fake Palestinian beggars in KL lately' (comments/1s2fp8q, 2025) document the donation-pitch pattern operating at temple/mosque perimeters. r/malaysia 'A random Malay guy just showed me his festering wound' (comments/125g9ue, 2023) is a canonical KL donation-beg anchor. The real Batu Caves is FREE to enter — there is no legitimate entrance fee to the Temple Cave (the main cave at the top of the stairs). The 2025 scam pattern: (a) a vendor at the stair base hands you a small flower garland, coconut, or prayer item — 'blessing from the temple, for Lord Murugan' — and when you try to hand it back at the top, insists on RM 30–RM 50 payment, sometimes physically blocking your descent until you pay; (b) unofficial 'photographers' at the stair base or the colourful stairs midpoint snap your photo unprompted then demand RM 20–RM 50 per 'copy' (which they print from a phone-to-Bluetooth printer or send via WhatsApp); (c) 'temple donation' touts at the Hanuman statue and the Dark Cave queue holding clipboards asking for RM 50–RM 200 donations — the actual temple donation is a voluntary drop-in at the marked donation boxes inside the Temple Cave; (d) parking-scam variant — unofficial 'parking wardens' at Jalan Batu Caves charge tourists RM 10–RM 20 for parking that is actually free or RM 2 in the official lot; (e) 'monkey-feed' vendors selling bags of peanuts at RM 10 (wholesale price under RM 1) then ignoring posted 'Do not feed the monkeys' signs; (f) overpriced coconut drinks (RM 15 vs fair price RM 5–RM 8) at stalls that hand the coconut to you before quoting; (g) Grab driver 'wait-and-tour' overcharges — r/KualaLumpur 'Scary Grab experience in KL' (comments/1npv0w4, 2025) documents a driver demanding RM 300 for a Batu Caves return trip that should cost RM 60–RM 80 total. For travelers: (1) take KTM Komuter from KL Sentral to Batu Caves station directly — RM 2.60 one way, 28 minutes, every 30 minutes — it's the cheapest, safest option; (2) if you want a taxi, book Grab round-trip with a planned 90-minute Batu Caves wait — the fair RM 60–RM 90 round-trip fare; (3) REFUSE every 'gift' handed to you at the stair base, including flowers, coconuts, prayer items, and blessings — hand them back immediately without touching your wallet; (4) there is NO entrance fee to the Temple Cave itself (the Dark Cave guided tour is separately RM 35 paid at the marked official counter); (5) if you want a photo of yourself on the rainbow stairs, ask another tourist or use a phone tripod — NEVER engage the stair photographers; (6) feed monkeys is strictly PROHIBITED by posted signs and poses a real bite-risk (Batu Caves macaques have been documented with Herpes B); (7) coconut water/drink stalls: ask the price FIRST — fair rate is RM 5–RM 8; (8) the legitimate way to give to the temple is the marked donation box inside the Temple Cave, NOT through anyone with a clipboard outside; (9) official parking in the paved lot adjacent to the cave base is RM 2–RM 5 for the day — refuse 'unofficial' parking offers at RM 10+.
scams.avoidance:
Take KTM Komuter from KL Sentral (RM 2.60, 28 min) — cheapest and scam-free option
Entry to the Temple Cave is FREE — there is no entrance fee
REFUSE every 'gift' handed to you at the stair base (flowers, coconuts, blessings)
Ignore unofficial stair photographers — ask another tourist for a photo
Coconut drinks should be RM 5–RM 8; confirm price before accepting
scams.location: Batu Caves 272 rainbow stairs, Hanuman and Lord Murugan statue areas, Temple Cave entrance, Dark Cave queue, stair base vendor strip, Jalan Batu Caves parking area, KTM Batu Caves station

scams.name: Fake MDAC (Malaysia Digital Arrival Card) Website RM 145 Immigration Scam
scams.description: Malaysia introduced the mandatory Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) on 1 January 2024, requiring ALL foreign visitors to submit an online arrival card within 3 days BEFORE entry — and within weeks a network of Google-ad-boosted counterfeit MDAC sites began harvesting payments from unsuspecting tourists. The legitimate MDAC is FREE and is filed ONLY at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my (official) — NEVER at any other URL. r/KualaLumpur 'I got scammed through malaysia digital arrival card' (comments/1i2uird, 2025) is the canonical 2025 first-person anchor. r/malaysia 'Scammed by fake Malaysia digital arrival card site' (comments/1i69qqa, 2025) documents the same pattern at scale. r/malaysia 'Don't fall for the MDAC scam' (comments/1otqtch, 2025) is a 2025 PSA thread. r/malaysia 'Hey visitors to Malaysia avoid a $94 scam' (comments/1rrk2gg, 2026) is the 2026 anchor — the scam is actively continuing. On 4 January 2025 New Straits Times published 'Immigration Dept warns tourists of fake MDAC website' and Malay Mail ran the same headline; on 13 February 2026 SoyaCincau published 'MDAC Scam in Malaysia: Tourist Charged RM 145 on Fake Site' — the scam sites charge between US$20 and US$94 (RM 90–RM 450) for a document that is free and takes 5 minutes on the official portal. The 2025–2026 scam pattern: (a) tourist Googles 'Malaysia digital arrival card' and the top sponsored/ad results are counterfeit sites like 'malaysia-mdac.com', 'mdac-online.org', 'malaysiaimmigration-arrival.com', 'mdac-gov.info', and dozens of rotating domain variants; (b) sites mimic the .gov.my look with Jalur Gemilang flag graphics, official-looking seals, and fake 'Immigration Department of Malaysia' branding; (c) forms capture full passport details, flight information, home address, and demand a 'processing fee' of RM 145 or equivalent (typical quoted prices: US$20, US$37, US$50, US$94) paid by credit card; (d) the site then emails a fake 'confirmation' PDF with a real-looking QR code; at Malaysian immigration the border officer finds no record, tourist is told to fill the real MDAC on the spot — identity data has already been sold to fraud rings; (e) card-on-file charges follow over the next 30–90 days; (f) some sites install cookie-based redirects that keep charging 'annual renewal' fees; (g) the Brunei MDAC scam warning reported in r/nasikatok 'BIBD warns against fake Malaysia MDAC website stealing' (comments/1hdq07h, 2024) shows cross-border reach; (h) on 7 October 2025 a single-mother KLIA2 taxi tout was fined RM 5,000 — the MDAC scam sits in the same tourist-extraction ecosystem. For travelers: (1) the ONLY legitimate MDAC URL is imigresen-online.imi.gov.my — type it directly, never click a Google ad or sponsored result; (2) the legitimate MDAC is absolutely FREE — no processing fee, no service fee, no 'premium' tier — if any site asks for payment, it is 100% a scam; (3) fill the MDAC yourself within 3 days before arrival; it takes about 5 minutes with passport, flight details, and Malaysian accommodation address; (4) if you fell for a scam site and paid, contest the charge with your bank IMMEDIATELY (within 24 hours) citing 'merchant fraud — impersonating government service'; file a police report at any PDRM station — IPD Dang Wangi +60 3-2697 2222 if you're already in KL — and submit to the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) by calling 997 (24/7 hotline since September 2025); (5) on arrival without an MDAC, you can still fill it at the airport immigration kiosk — it causes a 10–20 minute delay but does NOT deny entry; (6) identity-monitoring steps: change your passport.gov password, lock your credit file if offered, and watch for suspicious card charges for 90 days; (7) save the real MDAC FAQ at imi.gov.my for reference; (8) report the counterfeit domain to Google Ads (support.google.com) and to Malaysia's MCMC (Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission) at mcmc.gov.my/en/complaint — per The Star 'Malaysia scam losses rise to RM 2.7 bil in 2025, spike during festive seasons' and Malay Mail 'Police to operate 24-hour 997 hotline for scam victims from September' (26 July 2025), NSRC will coordinate with your bank for chargebacks within the first 24 hours of reporting.
scams.avoidance:
The ONLY legitimate MDAC URL is imigresen-online.imi.gov.my — type it directly
The legitimate MDAC is absolutely FREE — any site asking for payment is a scam
Fill the MDAC within 3 days before arrival; takes 5 minutes with passport and flight details
If scammed, call NSRC 997 (24/7) and your bank for chargeback within 24 hours
On arrival without MDAC, fill at the airport immigration kiosk — no denied entry
scams.location: Online (Google search results, counterfeit domains malaysia-mdac.com / mdac-online.org / mdac-gov.info and rotating variants), KLIA and KLIA2 immigration counters, border entry points at KL Sentral ETS arrivals
